subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the value of k, if the straight lines 6x−10y+3=0 and kx−5y+8=0 are parallel.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what parallel means for the two slopes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both slopes
steps.margin_note: First mark. Read each slope off its coefficients as −a/b. The second carries k, which the parallel condition will fix.
steps.memory_tip: Read each slope off its coefficients as −a/b; the second carries k.
lines: Slope of the line 6x − 10y + 3 = 0 is  m₁ = −a/b = −(6/(−10)) = 3/5
Slope of the line kx − 5y + 8 = 0 is  m₂ = −a/b = −(k/(−5)) = k/5

recall.must_convey: That m₁ = 3/5 and m₂ = k/5 are read off the coefficients.
accept: the slopes are three fifths and k over five
read both slopes as minus a over b
m one is three by five and m two is k by five

steps.why: Both slopes are needed before the parallel condition can be applied, and only one of them carries the unknown.
common_mistakes: Reading the slope as −6/10 by forgetting the sign of b.

steps.label: Equate the slopes
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Parallel lines have equal slopes, so setting m₁ = m₂ gives k at once.
steps.memory_tip: Parallel means EQUAL slopes, so m₁ = m₂ gives k at once.
lines: If the two lines are parallel then  m₁ = m₂

recall.must_convey: That parallel means m₁ = m₂, giving k = 3.
accept: parallel means equal slopes so k is three
set the slopes equal and solve
three fifths equals k by five so k is three

steps.why: Both denominators are 5, so the equation reduces to comparing the numerators directly.
common_mistakes: Using m₁m₂ = −1, which is the perpendicular condition.
